title: Light Intensity Controlled Smart Dimmer using LDR
abstract: Lights in rooms, corridors and streets often stay at full brightness even when enough daylight is available, wasting electricity. This project builds an automatic dimmer that measures ambient light with a light dependent resistor (LDR) and adjusts the brightness of LED lamps accordingly. An Arduino microcontroller reads the LDR through an analog input, maps the reading to a PWM duty cycle and drives the LEDs through a MOSFET, so the lamps brighten gradually as it gets darker and dim as daylight increases. A PIR motion sensor can switch lights to a low standby level when no one is present. The prototype is evaluated for energy savings compared with fixed-brightness lighting.

title: Automatic Street Light Control using LDR and Motion Sensing
abstract: Street lights that remain on all night at full power consume large amounts of energy on roads with little traffic. This project designs an automatic street lighting system that turns lights on at dusk using an LDR and dims them to a low level when the road is empty. Infrared or PIR sensors placed along the road detect approaching vehicles and pedestrians and raise the brightness of the next few lights ahead of them. A microcontroller coordinates the poles, and faulty lamps are reported to a central dashboard over a wireless link. The system reduces power consumption and maintenance effort compared with timer-based street lights.

title: Smart Irrigation System using Soil Moisture Sensors
abstract: Farmers often irrigate on fixed schedules, which wastes water and can harm crops. This project builds an automated irrigation controller that measures soil moisture, temperature and humidity using sensors connected to an ESP32 microcontroller and switches a water pump through a relay when the soil becomes too dry. Sensor readings are uploaded over Wi-Fi to a cloud dashboard where farmers can monitor field conditions and set moisture thresholds from a mobile phone. Weather forecast data is used to skip watering when rain is expected. The system reduces water usage and labour compared with manual or timer-based irrigation.

title: IoT Based Home Automation with Voice Control
abstract: Controlling household appliances manually is inconvenient, especially for elderly and disabled people. This project develops a home automation system in which lights, fans and other appliances are connected to relays driven by a NodeMCU board. Users control the appliances from a mobile app or by voice through Google Assistant or Alexa, using a cloud platform to relay commands. The system also supports schedules, shows the current state of every device, and reports energy usage. Sensors for temperature and motion allow automatic actions such as switching on the fan when the room is hot or turning off lights when nobody is present.

title: Smart Parking System using IoT Sensors
abstract: Searching for a free parking space in busy areas wastes time and fuel. This project builds a smart parking system in which ultrasonic or infrared sensors installed in each parking slot detect whether it is occupied. A microcontroller sends the slot status to a cloud server, and a mobile application shows drivers a live map of available spaces so they can drive directly to a free slot. The system can also reserve slots in advance and calculate parking fees based on duration. Occupancy history is stored to help administrators understand peak usage and plan capacity.

title: Gas Leakage Detection and Alert System
abstract: Leakage of LPG in homes, hotels and industries can cause fires and explosions. This project designs a gas leakage detector using an MQ-2 or MQ-6 gas sensor connected to a microcontroller. When the gas concentration exceeds a safe level, the system sounds a buzzer, switches on an exhaust fan, closes the gas valve using a solenoid, and sends an SMS or app notification to the owner through a GSM or Wi-Fi module. The sensor readings are logged for later analysis. The device is low cost and provides early warning that helps prevent accidents.

title: IoT Weather Monitoring Station
abstract: Accurate local weather information is useful for agriculture, campuses and smart cities, but commercial weather stations are expensive. This project builds a low-cost weather station that measures temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, rainfall and wind speed using sensors connected to an ESP8266 or ESP32 board. The readings are uploaded periodically to a cloud platform such as ThingSpeak and displayed on a web dashboard with graphs of historical data. Alerts are raised when conditions such as heavy rain or extreme heat are detected. Simple forecasting of short-term trends can be added using the collected data.

title: Smart Energy Meter with Real-Time Monitoring
abstract: Consumers usually see their electricity usage only once a month on the bill, which makes it hard to save energy. This project develops a smart energy meter that measures voltage and current with sensors, computes power and energy consumption on a microcontroller, and sends the data to a cloud server every few seconds. A mobile app shows real-time consumption, daily and monthly usage, and the estimated bill, and warns users when usage crosses a set limit. The meter can also cut off supply remotely through a relay, supporting prepaid billing and theft detection.

title: RFID Based Student Attendance System
abstract: Taking attendance manually in classrooms consumes lecture time and is prone to proxy attendance. This project designs an attendance system in which each student carries an RFID card that is scanned by a reader at the classroom entrance. A microcontroller reads the card ID, records the time and sends the entry to a central database over Wi-Fi. Faculty and administrators can view attendance reports through a web portal, and students with low attendance receive automatic alerts. The system speeds up attendance marking and keeps accurate records.

title: Smart Dustbin with Fill Level Monitoring
abstract: Overflowing garbage bins in cities cause hygiene problems, while collecting half-empty bins wastes fuel. This project builds a smart dustbin that measures its fill level with an ultrasonic sensor and opens its lid automatically when a person approaches. Each bin reports its level to a cloud server through a Wi-Fi or GSM module. A web dashboard shows the status of all bins on a map, and the system generates optimized collection routes so that trucks visit only bins that are nearly full. This improves waste collection efficiency and keeps public spaces clean.

title: IoT Based Fire Detection and Alarm System
abstract: Early detection of fire is essential to save lives and property. This project develops a fire detection system using flame, smoke and temperature sensors connected to a microcontroller. When fire is detected, the system triggers an alarm, activates a water sprinkler or pump, and sends alerts with the location to the owner and the nearest fire station through GSM or the internet. A dashboard shows sensor readings from multiple rooms or buildings. Combining several sensors reduces false alarms compared with single smoke detectors.

title: Water Tank Level Monitoring and Automatic Pump Control
abstract: Overhead water tanks frequently overflow or run dry because pumps are switched manually. This project designs a system that measures the water level in a tank using an ultrasonic sensor and automatically switches the motor pump on when the level is low and off when the tank is full. The current level is displayed on an LCD and on a mobile app, and users are notified of abnormal conditions such as a dry sump or pump failure. The system saves water and electricity and removes the need for manual monitoring.

title: Air Quality Monitoring System using IoT
abstract: Air pollution is a serious health concern in urban areas, but monitoring stations are few and far apart. This project builds a portable air quality monitor that measures particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and other gases using low-cost sensors connected to an ESP32. The device computes an air quality index and uploads readings to a cloud dashboard where data from multiple locations is shown on a map. Users receive alerts when pollution reaches unhealthy levels. The collected data can support awareness campaigns and local pollution studies.

title: Smart Door Lock with Fingerprint and OTP Authentication
abstract: Traditional key locks can be lost, copied or picked. This project develops a smart door lock that unlocks only for authorized users through fingerprint verification, a keypad PIN or a one-time password sent to the owner's phone. A microcontroller controls a solenoid lock and records every access attempt with a timestamp. The owner can grant temporary access to guests remotely through a mobile app and receives alerts on repeated failed attempts. A camera can capture images of people at the door for added security.

title: Vehicle Accident Detection and Alert System using GPS and GSM
abstract: Many road accident victims die because help does not arrive in time. This project designs an in-vehicle system that detects accidents using an accelerometer and vibration sensor connected to a microcontroller. When a sudden impact or rollover is detected, the system obtains the vehicle's location from a GPS module and sends an SMS with a map link to emergency contacts and nearby hospitals through a GSM module. A cancel button lets the driver stop false alerts within a few seconds. The system reduces emergency response time.

title: Wearable Health Monitoring System
abstract: Continuous monitoring of vital signs helps detect health problems early, particularly for elderly patients living alone. This project builds a wearable device that measures heart rate, blood oxygen saturation and body temperature using sensors such as the MAX30100 and a temperature sensor connected to a microcontroller. Readings are sent to a mobile app and a cloud server, where doctors and family members can view trends. Alerts are generated automatically when readings fall outside safe ranges, and a fall detection feature uses an accelerometer to call for help.

title: Smart Greenhouse Monitoring and Control
abstract: Plants in greenhouses need carefully controlled temperature, humidity, light and soil moisture. This project automates a greenhouse using sensors that monitor these conditions and actuators such as fans, sprinklers, heaters and grow lights controlled by a microcontroller. Set points for each crop are configured from a mobile application, and the system adjusts the actuators automatically to keep conditions within range. Readings are logged in the cloud so that growers can analyse how conditions affect yield. This reduces manual work and improves crop quality.

title: Smart Helmet for Two-Wheeler Riders
abstract: Many two-wheeler accidents involve riders who are not wearing helmets or are driving under the influence of alcohol. This project designs a smart helmet with a switch that detects whether it is worn and an alcohol sensor that checks the rider's breath. The bike ignition starts only if the helmet is worn and no alcohol is detected, communicating with a receiver on the bike over RF or Bluetooth. An accelerometer in the helmet detects crashes and sends the location to emergency contacts. The system encourages safe riding and speeds up help after accidents.

title: Obstacle Avoiding Robot using Ultrasonic Sensors
abstract: Autonomous navigation is a basic capability for mobile robots used in warehouses, homes and exploration. This project builds a wheeled robot that moves independently while avoiding obstacles. An ultrasonic sensor mounted on a servo scans the path ahead, and an Arduino decides whether to move forward, turn left or turn right based on the measured distances. DC motors are driven through an L298N motor driver. The robot can be extended with infrared sensors and a camera for better navigation, and it serves as a platform for learning embedded control and path planning.

title: Line Following Robot
abstract: Line following robots are used in industries and hospitals to move materials along fixed paths. This project builds a robot that follows a black line on a white surface using an array of infrared reflectance sensors. A microcontroller reads the sensors and uses a PID control algorithm to adjust the speed of two DC motors so that the robot stays on the line smoothly, including at curves and junctions. The robot can recognize stop markers and choose paths at intersections. Its speed and accuracy are tested on tracks of different shapes.

title: Solar Panel Monitoring with Dual Axis Sun Tracker
abstract: Fixed solar panels capture less energy because the sun's position changes throughout the day and year. This project builds a dual-axis solar tracker that uses four light dependent resistors to find the direction of maximum sunlight and two servo motors to orient the panel towards it. The panel voltage, current and power output are measured and uploaded to a cloud dashboard. The system compares the energy generated by the tracking panel with a fixed panel to show the efficiency gain, and alerts users when output drops due to dust or faults.

title: Cold Storage Temperature Monitoring System
abstract: Vaccines, medicines and perishable food must be stored within strict temperature ranges, and failures can go unnoticed overnight. This project develops a monitoring system that continuously measures temperature and humidity inside cold storage units and refrigerators using sensors connected to an ESP32. Readings are sent to a cloud server, and staff receive SMS and app alerts immediately when the temperature crosses safe limits or a door is left open. Historical logs support regulatory compliance and help identify failing equipment.

title: Smart Shopping Cart with Automatic Billing
abstract: Long billing queues at supermarkets waste customers' time. This project designs a smart shopping cart fitted with an RFID or barcode reader and a display. As customers add or remove products, the cart reads their tags, updates the running bill on the screen and checks the total against a budget set by the customer. At the end of shopping the bill is sent to a central server and paid online, so customers can skip the checkout counter. Store managers also receive real-time data about product demand and stock levels.

title: Women Safety Device with SOS Alert
abstract: Women travelling alone often need a quick way to call for help in unsafe situations. This project builds a compact wearable safety device with a panic button that, when pressed, sends an SOS message with the live GPS location to emergency contacts and the police through a GSM module or a paired smartphone. The device can also sound a loud alarm, record audio, and continue sharing location updates until the alert is cancelled. Pulse and motion sensors can trigger an alert automatically if a struggle is detected.

title: Flood Monitoring and Early Warning System
abstract: Floods cause loss of life and property, especially when residents receive late warnings. This project develops an early warning system that measures river and drain water levels with ultrasonic sensors and rainfall with rain gauges, connected to wireless nodes along the river. The data is sent to a central server that predicts rising water levels and issues alerts through SMS, sirens and a public dashboard when danger thresholds are approached. Historical data helps authorities identify flood-prone areas and plan evacuations.

title: Face Recognition Based Attendance System
abstract: Manual attendance is time-consuming and allows proxy attendance. This project develops an automated attendance system that recognizes students' faces from a classroom camera. Faces are detected using a model such as Haar cascades or MTCNN and recognized by comparing face embeddings generated with a deep learning model like FaceNet against a database of registered students. Recognized students are marked present in a database with a timestamp, and teachers can view and export attendance reports through a web interface. The system is evaluated for accuracy under varying lighting and poses.

title: Driver Drowsiness Detection System
abstract: Driver fatigue is a major cause of road accidents, especially during long night journeys. This project builds a system that monitors the driver's face through a camera and detects drowsiness in real time. Facial landmarks are used to compute the eye aspect ratio to detect prolonged eye closure and the mouth aspect ratio to detect yawning. When drowsiness is detected, the system sounds an alarm to alert the driver. It can run on a Raspberry Pi in the vehicle and is evaluated under different lighting conditions, including night driving with an infrared camera.

title: Plant Disease Detection from Leaf Images using CNN
abstract: Crop diseases reduce yield and farmers often cannot identify them early. This project trains a convolutional neural network on images of healthy and diseased leaves, such as the PlantVillage dataset, to classify common diseases of crops like tomato, potato and rice. Transfer learning with models such as ResNet or MobileNet improves accuracy with limited data. A mobile application allows farmers to photograph a leaf and receive the predicted disease along with treatment recommendations, working offline using a compressed model.

title: Handwritten Digit and Character Recognition
abstract: Recognizing handwritten text automates tasks such as processing forms, cheques and postal codes. This project builds a deep learning model that recognizes handwritten digits and characters. A convolutional neural network is trained on datasets such as MNIST and EMNIST, with preprocessing steps including normalization and data augmentation. A drawing interface lets users write characters on screen and see the predicted result instantly. The model's accuracy is compared with classical machine learning approaches such as support vector machines and k-nearest neighbours.

title: Traffic Sign Recognition for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous and driver-assistance systems must correctly recognize traffic signs to drive safely. This project trains a convolutional neural network on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark to classify traffic signs such as speed limits, stop and warning signs. Images are preprocessed with resizing, histogram equalization and augmentation to handle varying lighting and angles. The trained model is integrated with a real-time camera feed to detect and announce signs to the driver. Performance is measured by accuracy and inference speed.

title: Automatic Number Plate Recognition System
abstract: Manual recording of vehicle numbers at parking lots, toll plazas and gates is slow and error-prone. This project develops an automatic number plate recognition system that detects licence plates in images or video using an object detection model such as YOLO and reads the characters using optical character recognition. Recognized numbers are stored with timestamps in a database to log vehicle entry and exit, flag blacklisted vehicles and compute parking charges. The system is tested on Indian licence plates under different lighting and angles.

title: Sign Language Recognition and Translation
abstract: People who use sign language face communication barriers with those who do not understand it. This project builds a system that recognizes hand gestures of sign language from a webcam and converts them into text and speech. Hand landmarks are extracted using MediaPipe, and a machine learning or deep learning model classifies the gestures into letters and common words. The recognized text is displayed on screen and spoken using a text-to-speech engine. The system aims to provide a low-cost communication aid for deaf and hard-of-hearing people.

title: Facial Emotion Recognition using Deep Learning
abstract: Recognizing human emotions from facial expressions has applications in education, customer service and mental health. This project trains a convolutional neural network on the FER-2013 dataset to classify facial expressions into emotions such as happy, sad, angry, surprised, fearful, disgusted and neutral. Faces are detected in real time from a webcam and the predicted emotion is displayed on screen. The system can track emotional responses over time, for example to measure student engagement during online classes.

title: Object Detection Assistant for Visually Impaired People
abstract: Visually impaired people face difficulty navigating unfamiliar surroundings and identifying objects. This project builds an assistive application that uses a smartphone or wearable camera with an object detection model such as YOLO to identify obstacles, people, vehicles and everyday objects in real time. Detected objects and their approximate distance and direction are announced through audio feedback. Additional features include reading text aloud using OCR and recognizing currency notes. The system helps users move around more independently.

title: Brain Tumor Detection from MRI Images
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of brain tumors is critical for treatment, but manual analysis of MRI scans is time-consuming. This project applies deep learning to classify brain MRI images into tumor types such as glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor, or no tumor. A convolutional neural network with transfer learning is trained on public datasets, and segmentation models such as U-Net are used to outline the tumor region. Grad-CAM visualizations highlight the areas influencing the prediction to help radiologists verify results.

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection from Retinal Images
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of blindness, and early screening is limited by a shortage of eye specialists. This project trains a deep learning model to grade retinal fundus images into severity levels of diabetic retinopathy. Images are preprocessed to enhance contrast, and class imbalance is handled with augmentation and weighted loss. The model is deployed in a web application where health workers upload images and receive a severity grade and referral recommendation. Performance is measured using accuracy, sensitivity and kappa score.

title: Pneumonia Detection from Chest X-Ray Images
abstract: Pneumonia is a common and potentially fatal lung infection that is diagnosed using chest X-rays, which require expert interpretation. This project trains a convolutional neural network to classify chest X-ray images as normal or showing pneumonia, using transfer learning on public datasets. Data augmentation and class balancing improve generalization. Heatmaps highlight the lung regions that influenced each prediction. The system is intended as a decision support tool for doctors in areas with few radiologists.

title: Skin Cancer Classification using Deep Learning
abstract: Melanoma and other skin cancers are highly treatable when detected early. This project builds a deep learning model that classifies dermoscopic images of skin lesions into categories such as melanoma, nevus and basal cell carcinoma, trained on the ISIC dataset. Preprocessing includes hair removal and color normalization, and transfer learning with pretrained networks improves accuracy. A mobile application lets users photograph a lesion and receive a risk estimate with advice to consult a dermatologist.

title: Face Mask Detection System
abstract: Wearing face masks in public places helps reduce the spread of respiratory infections, but manual monitoring is difficult. This project develops a real-time face mask detection system that uses a camera feed to detect faces and classify whether each person is wearing a mask correctly, incorrectly or not at all. A lightweight convolutional neural network such as MobileNetV2 is trained on a labelled dataset, enabling deployment on low-power devices. The system raises alerts and logs violations at building entrances.

title: Crowd Density Estimation and Monitoring
abstract: Overcrowding at events, railway stations and temples can lead to stampedes. This project estimates crowd size and density from CCTV footage using deep learning models that generate density maps from images. The system counts people in real time, identifies areas that exceed safe density, and sends alerts to security staff. Historical data is used to predict peak crowd times. Accuracy is evaluated on public crowd counting datasets and on footage with varying camera angles and crowd sizes.

title: Fruit Quality Detection and Grading using Image Processing
abstract: Manual sorting of fruits by quality is slow and inconsistent. This project develops an automated grading system that captures images of fruits on a conveyor belt and classifies them by ripeness, size and defects using image processing and a convolutional neural network. Features such as color, texture and shape are extracted, and fruits are sorted into grades using a servo-controlled mechanism. The system improves sorting speed and consistency for farmers and food processing units.

title: Crop Yield Prediction using Machine Learning
abstract: Predicting crop yield in advance helps farmers and governments plan storage, pricing and food security. This project builds machine learning models that predict crop yield from historical data including rainfall, temperature, soil type, fertilizer use and crop variety. Algorithms such as random forest, gradient boosting and linear regression are compared. A web application allows farmers to enter their field conditions and receive a yield estimate along with recommendations for the most suitable crop for their region and season.

title: House Price Prediction using Machine Learning
abstract: Estimating the fair price of a house is difficult for buyers and sellers because it depends on many factors. This project builds regression models that predict house prices from features such as location, area, number of bedrooms, age of the building and nearby amenities. Data cleaning, feature engineering and handling of outliers are performed on a real estate dataset, and models including linear regression, random forest and XGBoost are compared. A web interface lets users enter property details and receive a price estimate.

title: Credit Card Fraud Detection
abstract: Credit card fraud causes large financial losses, and fraudulent transactions are rare compared with genuine ones. This project builds machine learning models that detect fraudulent transactions from features such as amount, time and anonymized transaction attributes. Because the data is highly imbalanced, techniques such as SMOTE oversampling and anomaly detection are used. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and autoencoders are compared using precision, recall and F1 score rather than accuracy. A dashboard flags suspicious transactions in real time.

title: Customer Churn Prediction
abstract: Retaining existing customers is cheaper than acquiring new ones, so companies need to identify customers likely to leave. This project builds machine learning models that predict customer churn for a telecom or subscription business using features such as usage patterns, complaints, contract type and payment history. Exploratory data analysis identifies the main factors behind churn, and models such as logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting are compared. The results are presented in a dashboard that helps the business target retention offers.

title: Stock Price Prediction using LSTM
abstract: Investors seek to anticipate stock price movements, which depend on complex patterns in historical data. This project uses deep learning to forecast stock prices from historical price and volume data. A long short-term memory (LSTM) network is trained on time series data obtained from financial APIs, and its predictions are compared with traditional methods such as ARIMA and linear regression. Sentiment from financial news headlines can be added as an extra input. Results are visualized in a web dashboard showing predicted and actual prices.

title: Heart Disease Prediction using Machine Learning
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death, and early risk assessment can save lives. This project builds machine learning models that predict the likelihood of heart disease from clinical attributes such as age, blood pressure, cholesterol, chest pain type and ECG results, using datasets such as the UCI heart disease dataset. Algorithms including logistic regression, decision trees, random forest and support vector machines are compared. A web application lets users enter their health parameters and receive a risk assessment.

title: Diabetes Prediction System
abstract: Many people with diabetes remain undiagnosed until complications develop. This project develops a machine learning system that predicts the risk of diabetes from attributes such as glucose level, BMI, blood pressure, insulin, age and family history, using the PIMA Indians diabetes dataset. Missing values are handled and features are scaled before training models such as logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost. The best model is deployed in a web application that provides a risk score and lifestyle suggestions.

title: Movie Recommendation System
abstract: With thousands of movies available on streaming platforms, users struggle to find content they will enjoy. This project builds a recommendation system that suggests movies based on user preferences. Content-based filtering recommends movies similar in genre, cast and plot to those a user liked, while collaborative filtering uses ratings from similar users, trained on the MovieLens dataset. A hybrid approach combines both methods. A web interface lets users rate movies and view personalized recommendations.

title: Suspicious Activity Detection in CCTV Surveillance
abstract: Security staff cannot continuously watch every CCTV camera, so incidents are often noticed too late. This project develops a system that analyses surveillance video to detect suspicious activities such as fighting, loitering, abandoned objects and intrusion into restricted areas. Deep learning models combining convolutional networks for spatial features with LSTM or 3D convolutions for motion are trained on public anomaly datasets. When suspicious activity is detected, the system alerts security personnel with a video clip of the event.

title: Fake News Detection using Machine Learning
abstract: Fake news spreads rapidly on social media and can mislead the public. This project builds a system that classifies news articles and social media posts as real or fake. Text is preprocessed and represented using TF-IDF features and transformer-based embeddings, and models such as logistic regression, LSTM and fine-tuned BERT are compared on datasets like LIAR and FakeNewsNet. A browser extension or web application lets users check an article and see the prediction with an explanation of the key words that influenced it.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Product Reviews
abstract: Companies receive large volumes of customer reviews that are impractical to read manually. This project performs sentiment analysis on product reviews from e-commerce sites to classify them as positive, negative or neutral. Text is cleaned and represented using word embeddings, and models such as Naive Bayes, LSTM and BERT are compared. Aspect-based analysis identifies opinions about specific features such as price, quality and delivery. A dashboard summarizes customer sentiment trends to help businesses improve their products.

title: Spam Email Detection
abstract: Spam emails waste users' time and are often used for phishing and fraud. This project builds a spam filter that classifies emails as spam or legitimate using natural language processing. Emails are preprocessed by tokenization, stop word removal and stemming, and represented with bag-of-words and TF-IDF features. Machine learning models including Naive Bayes, support vector machines and neural networks are trained and compared on public datasets. The best model is integrated into a simple email client to filter incoming messages.

title: AI Chatbot for College Enquiries
abstract: College offices receive repetitive questions from students and parents about admissions, fees, courses and events. This project develops a chatbot that answers such queries automatically through the college website and messaging apps. Natural language processing is used to understand the user's intent and extract key details, and answers are retrieved from a knowledge base of college information. Queries the chatbot cannot answer are forwarded to staff. The chatbot is available around the clock and reduces the workload on administrative staff.

title: Automatic Text Summarization
abstract: Reading long articles, reports and research papers takes considerable time. This project builds a text summarization system that generates concise summaries of long documents. Extractive methods select the most important sentences using techniques such as TF-IDF scoring and TextRank, while abstractive methods use transformer models such as BART or T5 to generate new sentences. The quality of summaries is evaluated using ROUGE scores. A web application lets users paste text or upload documents and receive summaries of adjustable length.

title: Resume Screening and Candidate Ranking using NLP
abstract: Recruiters spend significant time manually reviewing large numbers of resumes for each job opening. This project develops a system that automatically parses resumes, extracts skills, education and experience using natural language processing, and ranks candidates by how well they match a job description. Text similarity techniques such as TF-IDF and sentence embeddings compare resumes with job requirements. A web dashboard lets recruiters upload resumes, view ranked candidates and filter them by skills.

title: Voice Assistant using Speech Recognition
abstract: Voice assistants allow users to perform tasks hands-free using natural speech. This project develops a desktop voice assistant that recognizes spoken commands using speech recognition libraries and responds using text-to-speech. It can open applications, search the web, tell the time and weather, set reminders, play music and send emails. Natural language processing is used to identify the user's intent from the command. The assistant can be extended with custom commands and support for regional languages.

title: Hate Speech Detection on Social Media
abstract: Hate speech and abusive content on social media can harm individuals and communities, and manual moderation cannot keep up with the volume. This project builds a classifier that detects hateful and offensive posts using natural language processing. Datasets of labelled tweets are used to train models ranging from logistic regression with TF-IDF features to fine-tuned transformer models. Handling of slang, emojis and code-mixed language is addressed. A moderation dashboard flags harmful content for review.

title: Machine Translation between English and Indian Languages
abstract: Language barriers limit access to information for people who are not fluent in English. This project builds a neural machine translation system that translates text between English and an Indian language such as Hindi or Tamil. A sequence-to-sequence transformer model is trained or fine-tuned on parallel corpora, and translation quality is evaluated using BLEU scores. A web or mobile interface allows users to type or speak text and receive translations, with optional text-to-speech output.

title: Document Question Answering Chatbot
abstract: Finding specific information in long documents such as manuals, policies and textbooks is tedious. This project builds a chatbot that answers questions about uploaded documents. Documents are split into passages and converted into embeddings stored in a vector database, and the most relevant passages for a question are retrieved and passed to a language model that generates an answer with references to the source. Users can upload PDFs and ask questions in natural language through a web interface.

title: Plagiarism Detection System for Documents
abstract: Plagiarism in assignments and research papers undermines academic integrity, and manual checking is impractical. This project develops a system that detects copied and paraphrased content by comparing submitted documents against a database of existing documents and web sources. Text is preprocessed, and similarity is measured using techniques such as n-gram matching, cosine similarity of TF-IDF vectors and semantic embeddings. The system highlights matching passages and generates a similarity report with the sources.

title: Depression Detection from Social Media Posts
abstract: Many people with depression do not seek help, but their social media activity can show warning signs. This project uses natural language processing to identify signs of depression from social media posts. Linguistic features, sentiment and posting patterns are extracted, and models such as LSTM and BERT are trained on labelled datasets. The system is intended as an early warning tool that encourages users to seek support, with careful attention to privacy and ethical use of personal data.

title: Online Examination System
abstract: Conducting paper-based exams requires printing, invigilation and manual evaluation, which is slow and costly. This project develops a web-based online examination system where administrators create question banks and schedule tests, and students take timed exams from any device. Objective questions are evaluated automatically and results are published instantly with detailed analysis. Features such as randomized questions, tab-switch detection and webcam proctoring reduce malpractice. The system is built with a modern web framework and a relational database.

title: Hospital Management System
abstract: Hospitals handle large amounts of information about patients, doctors, appointments, billing and pharmacy stock, which is difficult to manage on paper. This project develops a web-based hospital management system that stores patient records, schedules appointments, manages doctor availability, generates bills and tracks medicine inventory. Different user roles such as administrators, doctors, receptionists and patients have their own dashboards. The system reduces paperwork, avoids errors and gives quick access to patient history.

title: Library Management System
abstract: Managing book issues, returns and fines manually in a library is time-consuming and error-prone. This project develops a library management system that maintains a catalogue of books, records issue and return transactions, calculates fines for late returns and sends due date reminders to members. Students can search for books, check availability and reserve them online. Barcode or RFID scanning speeds up transactions, and administrators can generate reports on popular books and inventory.

title: E-Commerce Website with Product Recommendations
abstract: Small businesses need an online presence to reach more customers. This project builds an e-commerce web application where customers can browse products, search and filter by category, add items to a cart, place orders and pay online through a payment gateway. Sellers manage products and orders through an admin dashboard. A recommendation engine suggests related products based on browsing and purchase history. The application is built using a full-stack framework with secure authentication.

title: College Event Management Portal
abstract: Organizing college events involves managing registrations, schedules, venues and communication with participants, often done through scattered spreadsheets and messages. This project develops a web portal where clubs create events, students browse and register for them, and organizers track registrations and attendance. Features include online payments for paid events, QR code tickets, notifications and certificate generation for participants. The portal centralizes event information and simplifies organization.

title: Canteen Food Ordering Application
abstract: Long queues at college canteens during breaks waste students' time. This project develops a mobile and web application that lets students view the menu, place food orders in advance and pay online. Canteen staff receive orders on a dashboard, update their status, and notify students when food is ready for pickup. The system also manages inventory and generates sales reports. It reduces waiting time and helps the canteen plan food preparation.

title: Blood Bank and Donor Management System
abstract: Finding blood donors quickly in emergencies is difficult, and blood banks struggle to track stock. This project develops a platform that maintains a database of donors with their blood group and location and tracks blood unit inventory at blood banks. Hospitals and patients can search for available blood or nearby donors and send requests, and donors are notified by SMS. The system reminds donors when they become eligible to donate again and alerts blood banks when stock runs low.

title: Online Voting System
abstract: Traditional voting requires voters to be physically present and involves manual counting, which is slow. This project develops a secure online voting system for elections such as college student council polls. Voters are authenticated using their credentials and a one-time password, and each voter can cast only one vote. Votes are stored securely and counted automatically, with results published instantly after polling closes. Administrators manage candidates and elections through a dashboard.

title: Personal Expense Tracker Application
abstract: Many people find it difficult to track their spending and stick to a budget. This project develops a mobile application where users record income and expenses by category, set monthly budgets and receive alerts when they approach their limits. Charts show spending patterns over time, and recurring expenses are added automatically. Transactions can be imported by reading bank SMS messages. The app helps users understand their finances and save money.

title: Job Portal Web Application
abstract: Job seekers and employers need an efficient platform to connect. This project develops a job portal where employers post vacancies and job seekers create profiles, upload resumes and apply for jobs. Search and filter features help users find jobs by location, skills and salary, and a recommendation feature matches candidates to suitable jobs. Employers can shortlist applicants and schedule interviews through the portal. The system is built with a full-stack web framework and secure authentication.

title: Real-Time Chat Application
abstract: Instant messaging is an essential communication tool. This project develops a real-time chat application that supports one-to-one and group conversations, with message delivery using WebSockets. Features include user authentication, online status, typing indicators, read receipts, file and image sharing, and message history stored in a database. End-to-end encryption can be added to protect privacy. The application is built with a modern web stack and is responsive on desktop and mobile devices.

title: Hostel Management System
abstract: Managing hostel room allocation, fees, complaints and visitor records manually is cumbersome. This project develops a web-based hostel management system in which students apply for rooms, wardens allocate rooms based on availability and preferences, and fees are tracked and paid online. Students can raise maintenance complaints and track their resolution, and the system records visitor entries and leave requests. Wardens and administrators get dashboards with occupancy and pending issues.

title: Campus Lost and Found Portal
abstract: Students frequently lose items such as ID cards, phones and books on campus, and there is no easy way to reunite them with their owners. This project develops a lost and found portal where users report lost or found items with descriptions, photos and locations. The system matches lost and found reports using keywords and categories and notifies the people involved. Ownership is verified before items are returned. The portal reduces the effort needed to recover lost belongings.

title: College Bus Tracking Application
abstract: Students often wait at bus stops without knowing when the college bus will arrive. This project develops a bus tracking system in which a GPS device or the driver's smartphone sends the bus location to a server in real time. Students view the live location of their bus on a map in a mobile app and receive notifications when it is approaching their stop. Administrators can monitor all buses, routes and delays. The system improves punctuality and safety for students.

title: Student Performance Analytics Dashboard
abstract: Teachers need timely insight into student performance to support struggling students. This project develops a dashboard that collects marks, attendance and assignment data and presents analytics such as performance trends, subject-wise comparisons and at-risk students. Machine learning models predict students likely to fail based on early performance indicators. Teachers and mentors receive alerts so they can intervene, and students can view their own progress. The dashboard is built with a web framework and charting libraries.

title: Doctor Appointment Booking Application
abstract: Patients often wait for long periods at clinics and find it hard to get appointments with specialists. This project develops a mobile and web application where patients search for doctors by specialization and location, view available slots and book appointments online. Doctors manage their schedules, view patient history and issue digital prescriptions. Reminders are sent before appointments, and video consultation is supported for remote patients. The system reduces waiting times and improves access to healthcare.

title: Crowdfunding Platform for NGOs and Social Causes
abstract: Non-profit organizations and individuals need a trustworthy way to raise funds for social causes. This project develops a crowdfunding web platform where verified NGOs create campaigns with goals and updates, and donors contribute through secure online payments. Donors can track how funds are used and receive tax receipts. Campaigns are verified by administrators to prevent fraud, and progress towards goals is displayed transparently. Social media sharing helps campaigns reach more donors.

title: Travel Itinerary Planner Application
abstract: Planning a trip involves researching destinations, transport, accommodation and activities across many websites. This project develops a travel planning application that generates personalized itineraries based on the user's destination, budget, duration and interests. It recommends attractions, estimates travel times between places using map APIs, and organizes daily schedules. Users can save, edit and share itineraries and see weather forecasts for their travel dates.

title: Farmer to Consumer Marketplace
abstract: Farmers often receive low prices for their produce because of middlemen, while consumers pay high prices. This project develops a marketplace application that connects farmers directly with consumers and retailers. Farmers list their produce with prices and quantities, consumers browse and place orders, and payments are processed online. The platform provides market price information and demand trends to help farmers decide what to grow and when to sell. Delivery coordination and ratings build trust between buyers and sellers.

title: Campus Carpooling and Ride Sharing App
abstract: Many students and staff travel to campus alone in their vehicles, increasing fuel costs, traffic and pollution. This project develops a ride sharing application where drivers offer rides along their route and passengers request seats. Matching considers route, timing and available seats, and users are verified with their institution credentials for safety. The app shows live location during rides, splits fuel costs and allows users to rate each other. It promotes sustainable and economical commuting.

title: Blockchain Based Certificate Verification System
abstract: Forged academic certificates are a growing problem, and verifying certificates manually is slow. This project develops a decentralized system on the Ethereum blockchain in which universities record a cryptographic hash of each issued certificate through a smart contract, while the documents are stored on IPFS. Employers verify a certificate by uploading it to a web portal that recomputes the hash and compares it with the blockchain record, confirming authenticity instantly without contacting the university. The system is tamper-proof and transparent.

title: Blockchain Based E-Voting System
abstract: Electronic voting systems must be secure, transparent and resistant to tampering. This project develops a voting system on a blockchain in which each vote is recorded as a transaction through a smart contract, making it immutable and verifiable. Voters are authenticated before voting, and each eligible voter can vote only once while their choice remains anonymous. Results are computed automatically and can be audited by anyone. The system is built with Ethereum, Solidity smart contracts and a web interface.

title: Supply Chain Traceability using Blockchain
abstract: Consumers and regulators find it difficult to verify where products come from and whether they are genuine. This project develops a blockchain-based supply chain system that records every stage of a product's journey from manufacturer to distributor to retailer. Each transfer is recorded on the blockchain, and products carry QR codes that consumers can scan to see their complete history. The system improves transparency and helps prevent counterfeit goods in sectors such as food and pharmaceuticals.

title: Land Registry Management using Blockchain
abstract: Land records maintained on paper are vulnerable to fraud, duplication and disputes, and property transfers involve lengthy procedures. This project develops a land registry system on a blockchain in which property ownership records and transfers are stored as tamper-proof transactions through smart contracts. Buyers can verify ownership history before purchase, and transfers are completed digitally with approval from the relevant authority. The system increases transparency and reduces fraud in property transactions.

title: Phishing Website Detection using Machine Learning
abstract: Phishing websites trick users into revealing passwords and financial details by imitating legitimate sites. This project builds a machine learning system that classifies websites as phishing or legitimate using features extracted from the URL, domain information and page content, such as URL length, use of IP addresses, SSL certificate details and domain age. Models such as random forest and gradient boosting are trained on public phishing datasets. A browser extension warns users before they enter information on suspicious sites.

title: Network Intrusion Detection System using Machine Learning
abstract: Computer networks face constant attacks such as denial of service, port scanning and unauthorized access. This project develops an intrusion detection system that monitors network traffic and classifies connections as normal or malicious using machine learning. Models such as random forest, support vector machines and deep neural networks are trained on datasets such as NSL-KDD and CICIDS. Detected attacks are reported on a dashboard with their type and severity so that administrators can respond quickly.

title: Secure Password Manager with Encryption
abstract: People reuse weak passwords across many accounts because remembering strong ones is difficult. This project develops a password manager that stores users' credentials in an encrypted vault protected by a master password. Data is encrypted using AES with keys derived from the master password, so the stored passwords cannot be read even if the database is stolen. The application generates strong passwords, autofills login forms through a browser extension and warns users about weak or reused passwords.

title: Image Steganography for Secure Communication
abstract: Sending sensitive information over public channels risks interception even when it is encrypted, because encrypted data attracts attention. This project develops a steganography application that hides secret messages inside images by modifying the least significant bits of pixel values, so that the change is invisible to the human eye. The message is encrypted before embedding for additional security. Users can hide and extract messages through a simple interface, and the quality of stego images is measured using PSNR.

title: Malware Detection using Machine Learning
abstract: Traditional antivirus software relies on known signatures and fails to detect new malware. This project develops a machine learning system that classifies executable files as malicious or benign using static features such as file headers, imported functions and byte n-grams, and dynamic features from behaviour in a sandbox. Models such as random forest, gradient boosting and neural networks are trained on public malware datasets. The system is evaluated on its ability to detect previously unseen malware samples.

title: Secure File Sharing System with Encryption
abstract: Sharing confidential files through email or public cloud storage risks unauthorized access. This project develops a secure file sharing system where files are encrypted on the user's device before upload using hybrid encryption with AES and RSA, so the server never sees the contents. Access is granted to specific recipients through their public keys, links can expire automatically, and every access is logged. Two-factor authentication protects user accounts.

title: Density Based Smart Traffic Light Control
abstract: Fixed-time traffic signals cause long waits at junctions even when some roads have little traffic. This project develops an adaptive traffic signal system that measures the vehicle density on each road using cameras with image processing or infrared sensors and adjusts the green signal duration accordingly. Roads with more vehicles receive longer green times, and emergency vehicles such as ambulances are detected and given priority. A simulation and a hardware prototype are used to show reduced waiting times compared with fixed-time signals.

title: Augmented Reality App for Interior Design
abstract: Customers find it difficult to imagine how furniture will look in their homes before buying it. This project develops an augmented reality mobile application that lets users place true-to-scale 3D models of furniture in their rooms using the phone camera. Built with ARCore or ARKit, the app detects floors and walls, lets users move, rotate and change the color of objects, and links to online stores for purchase. This helps customers make better buying decisions and reduces product returns.

title: Virtual Mouse using Hand Gesture Recognition
abstract: Controlling a computer without physical contact is useful for hygiene, accessibility and presentations. This project develops a virtual mouse that tracks the user's hand through a webcam and translates gestures into mouse actions. Hand landmarks detected with MediaPipe are used to move the cursor with the index finger, and gestures such as pinching are mapped to clicks, scrolling and dragging. Smoothing filters reduce jitter, and the system works with an ordinary laptop camera without any additional hardware.

title: Gesture Controlled Wheelchair
abstract: People with limited mobility may find it difficult to operate a joystick-controlled wheelchair. This project develops a wheelchair that is controlled by hand gestures using an accelerometer worn on the hand or glove. Tilting the hand in different directions moves the wheelchair forward, backward, left or right, with commands sent wirelessly to a microcontroller that drives the motors. Ultrasonic sensors stop the wheelchair automatically when obstacles are detected, and an emergency button alerts caregivers.

title: Drone Based Surveillance System
abstract: Monitoring large areas such as campuses, farms, borders and disaster sites with fixed cameras is difficult. This project develops a surveillance drone that flies along a planned path using GPS and streams live video to a ground station. Object detection models identify people, vehicles and unusual activity in the video feed and alert operators. The drone can be used for search and rescue after disasters and for monitoring areas that are difficult to reach on foot.

title: Electricity Load Forecasting using Machine Learning
abstract: Power utilities must predict electricity demand accurately to schedule generation and avoid shortages or waste. This project builds forecasting models that predict hourly and daily electricity load from historical consumption data together with weather, day of the week and holiday information. Models including ARIMA, random forest and LSTM networks are compared using error metrics such as MAPE. A dashboard displays forecasts and actual demand to support planning decisions.

title: IoT Based Water Quality Monitoring System
abstract: Contaminated drinking water causes many diseases, and laboratory testing is slow and expensive. This project develops a system that continuously monitors water quality parameters such as pH, turbidity, total dissolved solids and temperature using sensors connected to a microcontroller. Readings are uploaded to a cloud dashboard, and alerts are sent when parameters exceed safe limits. The system can be installed in water tanks, treatment plants and rivers to provide real-time information about water safety.

title: Smart Mirror with Voice Assistant
abstract: People often check the time, weather, news and their schedule while getting ready in the morning. This project builds a smart mirror using a two-way mirror placed over a display connected to a Raspberry Pi. The mirror shows the time, weather, news headlines, calendar events and reminders, while still functioning as a normal mirror. A voice assistant allows hands-free interaction, and face recognition shows personalized information for each family member. The software is modular so that new widgets can be added easily.
